summary: Iteration 4 — Streaming search normalization + word-boundary matching fully validated. Backend: 74/74 pytest passing (100%) = 18 phase-1 + 24 phase-2 + 12 phase-3 + 20 NEW phase-4. New phase-4 file covers BOTH integration (real /api/streaming/episodes calls with admin token) AND pure unit tests of _normalize_provider/_provider_matches helpers. Critical false-positive guard verified: Apple TV+ does NOT match 'Paramount Plus Apple TV Channel'. Critical false-negative guard verified: Disney+ DOES match 'Disney Plus' (returns Demolidor). Suffix matching ('Prime Video' → 'Amazon Prime Video', 'Max' → 'HBO Max') and prefix matching ('Netflix' → 'Netflix Standard with Ads', 'Paramount+' → all paramount* variants) all work. Frontend: iter-3 testid bug now FIXED — all 9 chip testids present with literal '+' (search-quick-disney+, search-quick-apple-tv+, search-quick-paramount+). Disney+ chip click flow end-to-end: input → 'Disney+', streaming-search-results visible, 1 streaming-episode-* card (Demolidor). All 8 other chips clicked without crash. Empty-state 'Nada por aqui ainda' renders correctly for chips with no matching admin shows (Apple TV+, Crunchyroll, Globoplay, Hulu). Zero pageerrors / zero console errors during the full chip sweep.

minor.issue: No caching of TMDB /tv/{id} responses — every search fires N parallel TMDB round-trips. Add 5-15 min in-memory cache keyed by tmdb_id (carried from iter-3).
Broad `except Exception` still returns 502 for some bogus sessions; spec compliance still met (returns 401 in main path) — carry-over note from iter-2/3.

critical_code_review_comments: GOOD: _normalize_provider() correctly handles '+' → 'plus' → '' so 'Disney+', 'Disney Plus', and 'disney plus' all collapse to 'disney'.

GOOD: _provider_matches() uses word-sequence prefix-OR-suffix equality on tokenized arrays — this elegantly avoids midword false positives (e.g., 'Maximum Streaming' won't match 'Max') AND sub-channel false positives (e.g., 'Paramount Plus Apple TV Channel' [tokens: paramount apple tv channel] does NOT have 'apple tv' at the start or end).
GOOD: Search.jsx line 110 testid generator now uses `replace(/\s+/g,'-')` so '+' is preserved in chip testids per the spec.
MINOR: _provider_matches treats the empty-needle case correctly (returns False) — good defense.

PERF: streaming_episodes() does asyncio.gather across the entire user library with no caching — cold latency scales linearly with library size. Acceptable for current 8-series admin lib but should be optimized before production scale.
STYLE: The streaming_episodes endpoint is ~70 lines; consider extracting the per-item match step into a helper for readability.

rca of the issue: Issue (from iter-3): backend was doing simple substring match — provider names like 'Disney+'/'Apple TV+' didn't match TMDB 'Disney Plus'/'Apple TV Plus'. Fix in iter-4 (verified): server.py:895 _normalize_provider() converts '+' → 'plus' word and then strips 'plus' tokens + punctuation → identical normalized strings for '+' and 'Plus' variants. server.py:910 _provider_matches() requires the needle's token sequence to appear as the prefix OR suffix of the provider's token sequence (or be exactly equal). This gives Disney+ ↔ Disney Plus equivalence AND blocks false positives like 'Paramount Plus Apple TV Channel' for an 'Apple TV+' search (tokenized as 'paramount apple tv channel' — 'apple tv' is mid-sequence, neither prefix nor suffix). Reproduction confirmed by 10 unit tests + 10 integration tests, all green.
